change.title: Rate-limit authenticated requests per client
change.summary: Adds a token-bucket rate limiter that runs on every authenticated request, sized by the client's plan. It replaces the ad-hoc five-orders-per-minute throttle that lived inside createOrder. Time comes from an injectable Clock so the limiter can be tested.
change.head: after

members.name: buildServer
members.summary: Wire the router: authentication, then rate limiting, then the order routes.
members.klar:
~ buildServer(clock = systemClock) → router
    router = create Router
+   limiter = create RateLimiter(clock)
    router.use(auth.requireAuth)
+   router.use(limits.rateLimit(limiter))
    router.get("/orders", orders.listOrders)
    router.post("/orders", orders.createOrder)
    Return router

    no effects

components.name: Router
components.summary: Matches requests to routes and runs them through the middleware chain.

members.name: use
members.summary: Append a middleware to the chain.

members.name: handle
members.summary: Find the route for a request and run it through every middleware in order.

members.name: requireAuth
members.summary: Reject requests without a valid bearer token; attach the user otherwise.
members.klar: requireAuth(request, next = rest of the chain) → response …

members.name: rateLimit
members.summary: Build a request step that turns a client away with 429 once their allowance runs out.
members.klar:
rateLimit(limiter) → request step(request, next = rest of the chain)
    If request has no user:
      Return next(request)
    decision = limiter.check(user.id, user.plan)
    If decision is denied:
      Return 429 + retry-after = decision.retryAfter
    Return next(request)

    no effects

components.name: RateLimiter

members.name: buckets
members.summary: One bucket per client ever seen; never evicted.
members.klar: state buckets = one TokenBucket per client, never removed

members.name: check
members.summary: Spend one token for this client, or say how many seconds until one is available.
members.klar:
check(client, plan) → allowed | denied
    now = clock.now()
    bucket = bucketFor(client, plan, now)
    bucket.refill(now)
    taken = bucket.tryTake()
    If taken:
      Return allowed
    Return denied + retryAfter = bucket.secondsUntilNext(), rounded up

    changes buckets · depends on time

members.name: bucketFor
members.summary: Find the client’s bucket, creating a full one from their plan’s limits the first time.
members.klar:
private bucketFor(client, plan, now) → bucket
    bucket = get buckets[client]
    If bucket is missing:
      limits = config.LIMITS[plan]
      bucket = create TokenBucket(limits.burst, limits.perSecond, now)
      add bucket to buckets for client
    Return bucket

    changes buckets

components.summary: Gives each client a token bucket sized by their plan.
components.klar:
+ class RateLimiter
    needs clock
    state buckets = one TokenBucket per client, never removed

components.name: TokenBucket

members.name: refill
members.summary: Add the tokens earned since the last refill, never exceeding capacity.
members.klar:
refill(now)
    elapsed = now − updatedAt, in seconds
    set tokens = min(capacity, tokens + elapsed × refillPerSecond)
    set updatedAt = now

    changes tokens, updatedAt

members.name: tryTake
members.summary: Take one token if a whole one is left.
members.klar:
tryTake() → yes | no
    If tokens < 1:
      Return no
    set tokens = tokens − 1
    Return yes

    changes tokens

members.name: secondsUntilNext
members.summary: How long until a whole token is available; zero if one already is.
members.klar:
secondsUntilNext() → seconds
    If tokens ≥ 1:
      Return 0
    Return (1 − tokens) ÷ refillPerSecond

    no effects

components.summary: An allowance that holds up to capacity tokens and regains refillPerSecond every second.
components.klar:
+ class TokenBucket
    needs capacity, refillPerSecond, now
    state tokens = capacity at start
    state updatedAt = now at start

components.name: Clock

members.name: systemClock
members.summary: Default implementation backed by the wall clock.

source.code: export const systemClock: Clock = { now: () => Date.now() };

members.klar: const systemClock = Clock that reads the system time

components.summary: Where the current time comes from; injected so rate limits can be tested.

members.name: LIMITS
members.signature: = burst and refill rate per plan
members.summary: How many requests each plan may burst, and how fast that allowance refills.
members.klar:
+ const LIMITS = burst size and refill rate for each plan
    free: burst 20, then 1 per second
    pro: burst 100, then 10 per second

components.name: orders

members.name: recentOrders
members.summary: Timestamps of each user's recent orders.
members.klar: - state recentOrders = order times for each user

members.name: createOrder
members.summary: Store a new order for the signed-in user.
members.klar:
~ createOrder(request) → 201 + order
-   remove times older than 1 min from recentOrders[user]
-   If recentOrders[user] has ≥ MAX_ORDERS_PER_MINUTE entries:
-     Return 429
-   add now to recentOrders[user]
    order = Wait for db.orders.insert(user.id, request.body)
    Return 201 + order

-   changes recentOrders · depends on time
    writes db

components.klar:
~ module orders
-   state recentOrders = order times for each user

flows.name: A request passes through the limiter
flows.description: Every authenticated request now spends one token before it reaches its route. An empty bucket ends the request with 429 and a retry-after header.

flows.name: Server start-up wiring
flows.description: buildServer creates one RateLimiter for the process and installs its middleware directly after authentication.

notes.text: Buckets are never evicted. Memory grows with every distinct client the process has ever seen.
Order creation is no longer capped at 5 per minute. It now shares the general allowance, so a free user can place 20 orders at once and then about 60 a minute.
The limiter runs after requireAuth, so unauthenticated requests are not limited at all.
Limits are held in process memory, so each server instance counts separately.
